scope: Primary statements and inherited theorem inputs actually used in the round-12 #1083/#827 geometry workflow.

sources.role: current OPEN statement of #1083, including the all-fixed-d quantifier and recorded three-dimensional lower-bound context
Rudnev--Selig, Theorem 2 (lines 59--66 in the arXiv HTML rendering): N points on S^2 or H^2 determine Omega(N/log N) distances; used for the O(D log n) spherical capacity in Theorem 4.6

Pach--Sharir, On the Number of Incidences Between Points and Curves (1998): the two-degrees-of-freedom point--curve incidence bound used after stereographic projection in (4.23b); its point-line specialization is also used in the affine/projective models of Theorem 4.11
Guth--Katz planar distinct-distance theorem; used for the O(D log n) capacity of a plane and hence the noncollinear rich-motion frame count
Rudnev point--plane incidence theorem inherited from rounds 9--11, with the projective line-pencil degeneration parameter
Kedlaya--Kolpakov--Poonen--Rubinstein, Theorem 1.2: pairwise rational-angle line configurations outside perpendicular configurations have at most 15 lines; used in Lemma 3.1
C. Martinez, Theorem 1.3: coefficient-uniform bounded-degree control of equidimensional torsion-closure parts for bounded-degree subvarieties of a fixed torus; used in Theorem 2.1
Viro, Theorem 5.A: relations among orthogonal hyperplane reflections are generated by involution and pencil relations; used only for the explicitly limited linear-part stress test
current OPEN statement of #827 and the recorded O(k^5) probabilistic upper bound
Martinez--Roldan-Pensado primary paper on distinct circumradii and the general-position formulation
current OPEN fixed-radius circle problem; its separate general-position O(N^(3/2)) target is mentioned only as an unresolved conditional interface

source_hypothesis_notes: The spherical-capacity use is invariant under translating and rescaling a nonzero Euclidean sphere; chord length and spherical angle are injectively related on [0,pi].

For kappa nonzero, the fixed-spherical-angle circles have two degrees of freedom with multiplicity at most two. The kappa=0 antipodal degeneration is not passed to Pach--Sharir: it is handled separately by projective point--line Szemeredi--Trotter.

Martinez is used only for a uniform degree bound on torsion closure. The exclusion of positive-dimensional torsion cosets is the separate inherited real one-parameter proof audited in INDEPENDENT_QA.md.
Viro applies only to linear parts and permits auxiliary mirrors; REPORT.md does not infer an original rich pencil from it.
warnings: No exhaustive novelty, priority, journal-quartile, or publication claim is made.

Theorem 4.6 is a potentially reusable few-distance rich-rigid-motion bound, but this workflow did not complete a dedicated isometry-energy literature review establishing that exact formulation as new.

The n^(9/20-o(1)) glide/fixed-point concentration in Theorem 4.11 is internally derived from elementary Euclidean/quaternion algebra and Szemeredi--Trotter, but no exhaustive novelty or priority search was completed for that structural formulation.
The noncommutative BSG/approximate-subgroup discussion is a future route, not an invoked theorem or proved consequence.
Neither original problem is closed and no recognized main exponent is changed.
